meta.title: Bright — AI emergency-scenario training
meta.description: An AI plays the patient or the doctor. You type what you'd actually do. Emergency-medicine roleplay drills for Android, free, built in the open by one developer.
meta.ogAlt: Bright — a step for your brighter future

hero.name: Bright
hero.tagline: A step for your brighter future.
hero.description: I'm building an AI training app for medical emergencies. The AI plays the patient — or the doctor — and you type what you'd actually do next.
hero.note: APK on GitHub Releases. There's no Play Store listing yet.

demo.label: Emergency session
demo.caption: An illustration of the interaction — not a recording of the app.

messages.text: It started twenty minutes ago. Feels like something heavy is sitting on me.
Vitals and a 12-lead ECG now. IV access, and chewable aspirin unless there's a contraindication.
BP 138/86, HR 102. The ECG shows ST elevation in II, III and aVF.
Inferior STEMI. Activate the cath lab and get a right-sided ECG.

what.title: Roleplay, not flashcards
what.lede: Bright puts you inside an emergency and keeps it moving. The AI stays in character; you answer in your own words.

cards.title: The AI takes the role
cards.body: It plays a patient in an emergency — or a doctor putting questions to you. The situation unfolds as a conversation, not a list of options.

cards.title: You write the response
cards.body: Nothing to pick from. You type what you'd actually say or do next, the way you'd have to in the room.

cards.title: Nothing vanishes when you leave
cards.body: Exit a session whenever you want. It's kept in your history, so you can read the whole thing back later.

what.note: History is stored on your device only. Google sign-in and cloud sync are on the roadmap, not in the app yet.

steps.title: Open Bright
steps.body: The first launch is a short cinematic intro: the name resolves, a few tutorial pages, then a language pick — Korean or English, guessed from your phone and changeable in settings.

steps.title: Start a session
steps.body: You're dropped into an emergency scenario with the AI already in character.

steps.title: Answer in your own words
steps.body: Type your response and the scenario moves on from what you said. Voice input is planned; today it's typing.

steps.title: Review it later
steps.body: Leave whenever you like. Every past session sits in your history, waiting to be read back.

design.title: Quiet on purpose
design.lede: This is a tool for practising emergencies. It should feel competent and calm — never loud.

points.title: Monochrome, all the way down
points.body: White, black, and the grays between. No accent color competing for attention while you're trying to think.

points.title: Your phone decides light or dark
points.body: Bright follows the system setting instead of asking. So does this site — with a manual toggle if you disagree.

points.title: Motion that answers you
points.body: Every button and slider animates. Nothing bounces, nothing lingers. It's there so a tap feels acknowledged.

points.title: A first launch worth watching
points.body: Name reveal, tutorial pages, language selection. It takes a few seconds and sets the tone for everything after it.

status.title: Built in the open
status.lede: One developer, shipping in small versions. Here's exactly where things stand — including what isn't built yet.

items.name: Android app
items.body: Install the APK from GitHub Releases. Free, no account needed.

items.name: iOS app
items.body: In active development with Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform, sharing the same core as the Android app.

items.name: Voice input
items.body: Speaking your answers instead of typing them. Designed, not shipped — no release has it yet.

items.name: Google sign-in and cloud sync
items.body: Your history is local to your device today. Signing in and syncing across devices is on the list.

items.name: Google Play
items.body: A submission was attempted before, but store distribution isn't being pursued right now. GitHub Releases is the real way to get Bright.

get.title: Install it from GitHub
get.lede: Android only for now, straight from the releases page. It's free — no paid tier, no ads, nothing to buy.
steps: Open the releases page on your Android phone.
Approve the install when Android asks — sideloaded apps need a one-time permission for your browser or file manager.
get.groqNote: The AI runs on Groq's free tier. Bright asks for a free Groq key the first time a session needs one — you can skip past it during setup. A page here to help you get and manage that key is planned.
